method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 75 covers C/D/E/F and sheet 76 covers F/G/H/I, so Ave F is the only shared corridor; both plates print 'AVE. F OR CHURCH' in this gutter and each prints the other's number beside it ('76' on sheet 75, '75' on sheet 76). The cross-street run changes hundred-block exactly here: sheet 75's block against the avenue reads 501/503/505/507/509/511 and 513/515/517/519/521/523 with evens 502-512 and 514/516/518/520/522/524; sheet 76's first block starts the next hundred at 601/603/605/607/609/611 and 613/615/617/619/621/623 with 602/604/606/608/610/612 and 614-624; the following avenue east on sheet 76 (Ave G or Winnie) begins 701/703/705/707 and 702/704/706/708. So 5xx->6xx is Ave F and 6xx->7xx is Ave G, one block east. The avenue frontage runs interlock at the same y: sheet 75's east block face carries evens 3702,3704,3706...3718 and sheet 76's west block face the odds 3701,3703,3705...3717, the two sides of the 37th-38th segment of Church.
note: Detection candidates (75: 2760/1743/726; 76: 744/1761/2778) are mid-block lines. '70'' is printed mid-avenue on both plates - at native x 3137 on sheet 75 and native x 163 on sheet 76 - which is itself the centre line; the block faces (sheet 75 west face 3038, sheet 76 east face 273) put the centre at 3143 and 168 respectively, so 3143 / 166 are recorded. The avenue carries R.R. sidings on both plates, drawn 50-110 px in from its east face on each, consistent across the seam.
